caption: What if you fell into Jupiter? Its gravity would pull you in at about 200,000 km/h before you even reached the clouds. Then the shock: there is no ground. Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium gas, and gravity at the cloud tops is about 2.5 times Earth's, so a 40 kg kid would feel like 100 kg. Winds blow at about 650 km/h, and the Great Red Spot is a storm about 1.3 times wider than our whole planet. NASA's Galileo probe tried this in 1995 and lasted 58 minutes before heat and pressure won. Deeper still, hydrogen gets squeezed into a liquid metal, and the centre may reach about 24,000 °C, hotter than the Sun's surface. In India, Jupiter is Guru, which is why Thursday is Guruvar. Plot twist: in 2003 NASA crashed the Galileo spacecraft itself into Jupiter on purpose, so Earth germs could never reach the icy moon Europa. Would YOU take the plunge? 👇
